title: Algebraic cancellation inequality
statement: Let $m,k$ be nonnegative integers and $A,B,M,C,D$ be real numbers. Suppose $B>0$, $C\ge 1$, $CD=1$, $(D^kB)^{2m+1}\le M^{2(m+1)}$, and $M^{2(m+1)}\le A^2B^{2m}$. Then $B\le (C^{m+1})^{2k}A^2$.
replaced: Let $m,k\ge0$ be integers and $A,B,M,C,D$ be real numbers with $B>0$, $C\ge1$, and $CD=1$. If $(D^kB)^{2m+1}\le M^{2(m+1)}$ and $M^{2(m+1)}\le A^2B^{2m}$, then $B\le(C^{m+1})^{2k}A^2$.
